listenings.text: So, a normal week here. Monday to Friday I get up at half past five, because the good waves are before school and school starts at nine. I catch the bus at ten past eight and I use my bus pass, which my host family sorted out in the first week. At the moment I am doing an assignment on Australian history, which is due Friday, and I have not started it properly yet. Last weekend I worked at the surf shop for the first time. This weekend I am going to work again, and then I am going to sleep for about eleven hours.

Every exchange student I have met says the same thing about the first month. Week one is a holiday. Week two is horrible, and that is when most of them call home crying. Week three something switches. And by week four they have a routine and they have stopped translating everything in their head. My advice is simple. Join something in the first seven days, anything, and say yes to every invitation for a month even when you are tired. The ones who settle in fast are not the ones with the best English. They are the ones who left the house.

items.situation: Describe your school-day routine in three sentences.
Somebody asks what you are doing right now, and what you are doing this week.
Somebody asks what you did last weekend. Two sentences, finished time.
Somebody asks how long you have been here and what has changed.
Somebody asks about next weekend. Two decided plans.
